page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an Arm-based general-purpose compute instance equipped with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance is powered by dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 physical cores clocked at 3.0 GHz, featuring 1 thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and an 80 MB shared L3 cache. Cryptographic operations are supported via hardware-level AES instructions. Bundled with the instance is 1,608 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage distributed across four local drives. It does not include hardware GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong raw memory throughput and integer performance. The system achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory testing (3,247.82) alongside strong uncached large-block read (314.24 GB/sec) and write (120.6 GB/sec) memory bandwidth. CPU evaluations via Geekbench yield strong results for both single-core (1,961.0) and multi-core (17,040.0) metrics, matching high throughput in gzip compression (32.37 GB/sec) and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression (221.45 GB/sec). Standard multi-core stress testing via stress-ng (29,085.33), PassMark CPU scoring (16,147.55), software compilation, and ray tracing fall within the middle 50% average range. Small LLM text generation shows strong performance at 320.15 tokens per second, though medium 7B model generation settles into average ranges (22.17 tokens per second).

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated Neoverse-V2 cores offer stable compute density paired with exceptional memory throughput per vCPU. The integrated 1,608 GB NVMe SSD storage eliminates the network latency inherent to external block storage, making this profile advantageous for I/O-sensitive pipelines. Tradeoffs center on the lack of x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX-512 or AMX, alongside the absence of discrete GPU acceleration, limiting its efficacy for heavy matrix math and large-scale model training. The instance is best suited for transactional and analytical databases, high-throughput caching layers like Redis, continuous integration and build pipelines, data compression tasks, and localized file-heavy web serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose server powered by 16 dedicated ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 physical cores operating at 3.0 GHz and 64 GB of memory. It features 1,608 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage across 4 drives and contains no GPU accelerators. The instance achieves top-tier memory benchmark scores (PassMark memory score of 3,247.82) and strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 314 GB/sec read and 120 GB/sec write. Single-core and multi-core Geekbench scores place in the top quartile, supported by robust hardware AES cryptography and balanced multi-threaded decompression performance. Lacking x86 vector extensions like AVX-512, it trades specialized vector math for power-efficient dedicated core density and high local storage IOPS. This profile is well suited for database operations, in-memory caches, software compilation, data compression, and I/O-intensive enterprise workloads.
